baseline_final_answer: The WebSphere Application Server transactions are rolled back because of stale database connections caused by various factors such as database crashes, timeouts, or other events that invalidate the connection. These stale connections lead to the `com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException` which is further escalated to a `java.sql.SQLRecoverableException`. The root cause of this issue lies in the fact that the connection is no longer valid when the transaction attempts to reuse it, resulting in a rollback of the transaction.

Title: IBM Demystifying the WebSphere StaleConnectionException - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 What is the StaleConnectionException, why is it issued by WebSphere Application Server, and what should be done about it? 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
In WebSphere Application Server, the StaleConnectionException is issued when the database vendor issues an exception indicating that a connection currently in the connection pool is no longer valid. This can happen for many reasons, including: 

 * The application tries to get a connection and fails, as when the database is not started.
   
   
 * A connection is no longer usable due to a database failure. When an application tries to use a connection it has previously obtained, the connection is no longer valid. In this case, all connections currently in use by an application can get this error when they try to use the connection.
   
   
 * The application using the connection has already called close() and then tries to use the connection again.
   
   
 * The application tries to use a JDBC™ resource, such as a statement, obtained on a now-stale connection.

If an event occurs outside of the WebSphere Application Server to cause the connection to become invalid, such as a firewall connection timeout, database server drop, or network problem, when the WebSphere application attempts to re-use the connection and discovers the connection is no longer valid, the SCE results.

How do I configure TLS/SSL for an IIB web service provider and consumer?

I'm investigating ways and technologies for use with IIB to run a web service that runs as both a provider and consumer. I'm looking at HTTP and SOAP messages/nodes. At a high level it might look like this:
HTTPInput (TLS over HTTPS) -> Compute -> HTTPRequest (SSL over HTTPS) -> Compute -> HTTPReply
or
SOAPInput (TLS over HTTPS) -> Compute -> SOAPRequest (SSL over HTTPS) -> Compute -> SOAPReply
Does anyone have more details/references beyond the knowledge center on how to configure the TLS/SSL portions?
baseline_final_answer:
To configure TLS/SSL for an IIB web service provider and consumer, you need to ensure that both the controller web servers and the network load balancer (NLB) appliance are configured to use the same SSL certificate. This is because both the controller web servers and the NLB appliance will be communicating over HTTPS.

For more detailed information on configuring Controller Web to use SSL (HTTPS), refer to IBM Technote #1998458, which can be found at http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21998458.

baseline_final_answer: Yes, it is possible to remove the KD4SoapHeaderV2 header appearing in the Web Services messages after enabling ITCAM for SOA DC. PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The SOA D4 Agent was configured for the WebSphere Data Power appliance, which initially used SSLv3. Communication to the Data Power Appliance was changed to TLS, but the SOA agent still attempts to connect using SSL. 

SYMPTOM
The startDC.sh/startDC.bat passes the following Java Parameter during the startup of the SOA DC, 


"-Djava.protocol.handler.pkgs=com.ibm.net.ssl.www.protocol"

This parameter is what causes the SSL communication via the version of JAVA the customer uses when running the startup script.


DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Determine your JAVA version prior to running the startDC.sh/startDC.bat script by running 'java -version'. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
APAR IV66110 (updated with IV68808) implement the POODLE 
(CVE-2014-3566) fix which uses a default TLS rather than SSLv3 protocol.

If you are using a jre not containing IV66110 please see the following 
document, section "Alternative mitigation options"
